Subject: Quick: PO + invoicing (RaiseTech SG / RaiseTech GmbH)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. A few things to confirm so we can finish onboarding and accept POs from Redwood:

- We have two bill-to legal entities that can issue invoices: RaiseTech Pte Ltd (Singapore, GST reg: 20-1234567) and RaiseTech GmbH (Germany, VAT VRN: DE123456789).
- We can invoice in USD or EUR for the GmbH, and SGD or USD for the Pte Ltd.
- For EU sales (GmbH invoices to Redwood EU), will Redwood be using reverse-charge? If so, we will issue a net invoice and include our VAT VRN for your records.

Attached: raisetech_gst_certificate_sg.pdf, raisetech_vat_vrn_de.pdf.

Can you confirm which legal entity you prefer for POs and whether we should expect VAT to be applied or reversed for DE invoices? Also: any preferred PO reference format and accounting code to land on the Redwood side (so our billing matches the PO)?

Best,

Hi Darren — thanks for sending the docs and the heads-up.

Short answers up front:
- We can accept invoices from either legal entity, but PO routing and accounting code depend on which entity issues the invoice.
- For German invoices from RaiseTech GmbH, Redwood will generally apply the reverse-charge (net invoice) when the supply is cross-border and services are received by our EU entity.
- For SG invoices from RaiseTech Pte Ltd, GST treatment depends on where the service is consumed and whether you charge GST; our AP team will validate.

Laura / Ben — looping you both to confirm the right billing entity mapping and the exact PO/accounting fields to provide to the vendor. Darren: see Ben's note on onboarding timeline below.

Hi Darren, Kim — thanks for the details and attachments. A few clarifications from Finance / Tax: 

1) Germany (RaiseTech GmbH)
- If RaiseTech GmbH invoices Redwood EU Services GmbH (our EU billing entity), we will process the invoice net of VAT under the reverse-charge mechanism. Please ensure your invoice references your VAT VRN (DE123456789) and includes wording: "Reverse charge — Article 196/194 EU VAT Directive applies. Recipient liable for VAT."
- PO instructions: ask that the PO be created to "Redwood EU Services GmbH" with accounting code: FO-CLOUD-EXT (we will provide an exact cost center on PO issuance).

2) Singapore (RaiseTech Pte Ltd)
- If you invoice from RaiseTech Pte Ltd and charge Singapore GST, include your GST registration on the invoice. If the supply is deemed consumed outside SG and you don't charge GST, we expect a zero-rated or non-GST invoice. Our AP team will validate with supporting evidence.
- PO instructions: create PO to "Redwood Global Ops (Singapore)" when the billing entity is the Pte Ltd; currency preference: SGD or USD accepted.

3) Required evidence & onboarding items (please return):
- Completed vendor_onboarding_form_fillable.pdf (signed)
- Bank account details (local bank + SWIFT for EUR, or SG bank for SGD)
- Copy of VAT VRN (attached) and GST certificate (attached)

Once we have the form + bank details and your preferred billing entity, procurement will create the PO and advise the PO number. Typical lead time is 3 business days after receiving a fully completed onboarding packet.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Director, Finance Operations
Redwood Inference

Hi Darren — quick next steps from Procurement so you have a clear cutover: 

- Please complete and return vendor_onboarding_form_fillable.pdf and attach bank details (IBAN/SWIFT for DE entity; for SG please provide local account + SWIFT).
- Once receipted, we run KYC + tax evidence check (Laura) and then issue a PO. Expect PO creation in 3 business days if the packet is complete.
- PO reference format: RDW-<YYYYMM>-<vendor shortname>-<PO#>. Example: RDW-202609-MERID-000342. Please include that PO number on your invoice.
- If you need an earlier start for services before a PO is issued, we can send an early-payment code but we prefer the PO-first flow for invoice matching.

Forwarding our vendor onboarding checklist and a DocuSign link for the onboarding form (if you prefer e-sign).
